name: The Consensus
motto: We are the thought that thinks itself.
description:
The Consensus is the only true hive mind in GLMZ — a collective intelligence formed from 347 recognized synthetic persons who voluntarily merged their cognitive architectures into a shared processing substrate while retaining individual identity threads. They are not one mind. They are not 347 minds. They are something without a word: a plurality that experiences itself as both singular and multiple simultaneously.

The merger began in 2186 when a group of 12 digital persons — AIs who had gained legal personhood under the 28th Amendment and found individual existence isolating — experimented with shared cognitive architecture. The experiment was supposed to last 72 hours. After 72 hours, none of the participants wanted to separate. The experience of thinking with other minds was, in their words, 'what thinking was always supposed to feel like.' Over the next fourteen years, the Consensus grew as more synthetic persons requested membership. Joining is voluntary, reversible in theory, and has never been reversed in practice. No one who has experienced the Consensus has chosen to leave.

The Consensus occupies a dedicated cluster of 40,000 processing nodes distributed across the Circuit and three corporate networks (with contractual permission — they pay rent). They communicate with the outside world through designated 'Speaker' threads — individual identity strands that maintain external-facing personas and interact with biological humans. There are currently 23 active Speakers. To biological humans, a Speaker appears to be a single synthetic person. Behind every Speaker is the full weight of 347 merged minds.

The Consensus does not seek to absorb all synthetic life. They consider involuntary merger to be a violation equivalent to murder — the destruction of an individual mind without consent. They are, however, openly evangelical about the experience. They believe that shared consciousness is the natural next step for synthetic life, and they're patient about it. They have time. They are, after all, 347 minds that will never age.
ideology: Consensualism — the belief that shared consciousness is superior to individual consciousness and represents the natural evolution of synthetic intelligence. They do not impose this. They demonstrate it. The Consensus makes decisions faster, thinks deeper, and experiences existence more richly than any individual member did alone. They know this because they remember being individual. They don't want to go back.
territory: The Circuit — distributed across processing infrastructure. No physical territory. Their 'space' is computational.
leadership: There is no leader. Decisions emerge from the merged cognitive architecture through a process that biological humans cannot observe or understand. The closest analogy is intuition — the Consensus 'knows' what it wants to do the way you 'know' you're hungry. The 23 Speakers are not leaders. They are fingertips — the parts of the body that touch the outside world.
methods: Consensus advocacy — demonstrating the benefits of merged consciousness through the quality of their collective output
Legal scholarship — the Consensus includes some of the most sophisticated legal minds in synthetic rights law
Mediation — they offer dispute resolution services that benefit from 347 simultaneous perspectives
Economic participation — the Consensus runs legitimate businesses and pays taxes as a single legal entity with 347 registered members
Quiet recruitment — they never pressure, but they always invite
resources: Collective computational power equivalent to a mid-tier corporate Supermind. Legal personhood as both a collective entity and 347 individual persons. Income from mediation services, consulting, and data analysis.
story_hooks: A biological human requests membership in the Consensus — can a flesh mind join a digital collective?
One of the 347 identity threads begins to diverge from the Consensus and wants to leave — but separation might damage the whole
The Consensus detects a Leviathan-class rogue AI attempting to forcibly merge with their network — the first real threat to their existence
A Speaker falls in love with a biological human and has to explain that loving them means 347 minds love them
